messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for release v2.14 -> canary-set=canary-5, 10% traffic. health checks enabled.

maria (oncall): Got paging alert — canary-5 5xx spike (~12%) and p95 latency ~3x baseline. Aligning thrusters. :rotating_light:

incident-bot: INCIDENT P2437 created · Severity: S2 · Paging oncall (maria). Incident channel: #incidents · Incident lead: maria.

maria (oncall): Quick check: grafana dashboard -> https://grafana.redwood/company/d/abcd/canary-health?orgId=1&var-canary=canary-5

raj (sre): Looking at infra metrics. CPU on proxy nodes jumped, connection errors to token-service. Can someone confirm if the new-token-cache flag was on for this canary?

henry (eng): Yes, feature flag `new-token-cache` was enabled in this rollout for canary-5. I can flip it if that looks likely.

lisa (support): Support queue: 12 active tickets referencing 502s from API. 2 are enterprise customers. They're asking for ETA.

maria (oncall): Please flip the flag first — low-impact attempt. Command via FF service: 

```
curl -X POST "https://ff.redwood/api/v1/toggles/new-token-cache/override" 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_API_TOKEN" 
  -d '{"environment":"canary-5","value":false}'
```

henry (eng): Flipped the flag to false for canary-5. Confirmed via FF UI.

maria (oncall): Monitoring... error rate dropped from 12% -> 7% in last 30s but still elevated. p95 still high.

raj (sre): Logs show stale KV entries in token cache backing service. Looks like the flag flip disabled new caching logic but instances are still serving cached state. Need to restart token-service pods for canary-5 and clear local caches.

henry (eng): Restarting token-service on canary nodes now: 

```bash
kubectl -n prod-canary-5 rollout restart deploy/token-service-canary
```

henry (eng): Also evicting local proxy cache entries for canary: 

```bash
# careful: targeted to canary namespace only
redis-cli -h redis-canary.local -n 1 --scan | xargs -L 100 redis-cli -h redis-canary.local -n 1 del
```

maria (oncall): Heads-up: deploy-bot reports automated rollback triggered but aborted due to DB migration lock.

deploy-bot: Automated rollback attempt for v2.14 -> previous (v2.13) aborted: migration_lock_detected on migration_service (lock_id=9876). Manual coordination required.

raj (sre): If automated rollback is blocked, we should shift traffic off the canary instead of full rollback. Initiating manual traffic shift to baseline: 

```
# move canary-5 to 0% traffic in routing service
rbctl route set --canary canary-5=0%
```

henry (eng): Routing change applied. Canary traffic now at 0%. Baseline (v2.13) receiving the diverted requests.

maria (oncall): Post-shift metrics: error rate back to ~1.4% (baseline), p95 latency near normal. Looks stable for now.

lisa (support): Notifying impacted customers with short status update. Draft: "We're investigating errors related to a canary deployment; traffic has been shifted back to baseline and we're monitoring. We'll follow up with root cause." Sending now to enterprise contacts.

incident-bot: Incident P2437 status -> mitigated. Pager: standby cleared. Please run a postmortem and tag with customer-impact.

maria (oncall): Agreed — I'll open postmortem. Action items: (1) verify migration lock handling in rollback workflow, (2) add canary cache eviction step to rollout runbook, (3) run a game-day to exercise manual traffic shift.

henry (eng): Will follow up on runbook edits + add automated cache-invalidator that runs on flag flips.

raj (sre): I'll add a guard in the automated rollback flow so lock presence triggers traffic-shift fallback instead of abort.

lisa (support): Closing out customer comms here, will provide a timeline once postmortem ready.

maria (oncall): Closing thread — thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
